scope: Strict parent-to-child machine-principal attenuation, bounded recursive lineage metadata and Ed25519 provenance attestations. The slice is non-production-reachable and does not authorize spawning or promote a capability.
core_invariant: A lineage artifact may prove that an issuer attested to a bounded parent-child proposal. It cannot increase machine authority, authorize execution, prove runtime spawn, transfer trust, prove task success or establish global currentness.

risks: child receives a larger request rate
child receives larger request or response budgets
controls: component-wise child<=parent checks across all current v1 machine budgets

risks: descendant increases child or descendant count ceiling
controls: lineage depth must increment exactly by one
exact parent attestation digest required after generation one

risks: machine parent is substituted for required human sponsor
controls: parent and child must share the same human sponsor
existing v1 knownHumanPrincipals validation remains in force
parent is recorded as causal lineage only

risks: lineage appears to recurse while retaining one identity
controls: parent and child IDs must differ
principal definition and authority digests are separately bound
child expiry cannot exceed non-persistent parent expiry
proposal expiry cannot exceed child expiry

risks: previous child is not the next parent
controls: exact previous-child to next-parent principal-definition digest binding
issuer key ID derived from canonical public key

risks: trusted parent causes child to be marked trusted
signed lineage is marketed as output verification
historical provenance is treated as reputation
controls: no reputation field or trust score

risks: spawn proposal used as bearer capability
lineage attestation treated as permission to execute
agent invokes tools because ancestry is valid
valid historical lineage is treated as current authority
attestation is replayed to recreate work
controls: production currentness/revocation admission is an explicit future gate

risks: laboratory code described as supported dynamic spawning
controls: design and threat model repeat non-production boundary

known_nonclaims: The v0 laboratory does not authorize a runtime to spawn a child.
The v0 laboratory does not issue child machine identity credentials.
The v0 laboratory does not prove that a child process existed or executed.
The v0 laboratory does not prove task success, output correctness or truth.
The v0 laboratory does not establish reputation or inherit trust.
The v0 laboratory does not establish global authority, revocation or identity currentness.
The v0 laboratory does not permit machine principals to change axiom-machine-principal.v1 delegation semantics.
The v0 laboratory does not enforce actual runtime token/storage/descendant consumption; it validates declared ceilings only.
The v0 laboratory does not promote a capability or add a production route.
next_gates: root/sponsor spawn authorization primitive separate from the v1 principal definition
child credential issuance and currentness binding
